data.title: Hand eczema & pompholyx — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Hand eczema & pompholyx** (Eczemas)_

**Q1. Why is hand eczema important?**
- Commonest occupational skin disease (prevalence ~10% in general population, much higher in wet workers — health workers, cleaners, hairdressers, cooks, construction); chronic, causes job loss and poor quality of life

**Q2. Classify hand eczema.**
- By cause: irritant contact (commonest), allergic contact, atopic hand eczema, protein contact dermatitis/contact urticaria, combinations
- By morphology: pompholyx (recurrent vesicular), hyperkeratotic (palmar), fingertip (pulpitis), nummular, apron (proximal palm and adjacent fingers), chronic fissured, ring dermatitis, wear-and-tear (dorsa)
- Acute (<3 months) vs chronic (>3 months or ≥2 relapses/year)

**Q3. What is pompholyx (dyshidrotic eczema)? (PYQ)**
- Recurrent crops of deep-seated, itchy, tense vesicles ('sago-grain'/tapioca) on sides of fingers and palms ± soles; may form bullae; dry to brown spots and peeling in 2–3 weeks
- Triggers: hot weather, sweating, stress, atopy, nickel/cobalt systemic exposure, dermatophyte id reaction, IVIG, smoking
- Not a disorder of sweat glands despite the name

**Q4. Differential diagnosis of vesicular hand eczema.**
- Tinea manuum/id reaction (look at feet, KOH), palmoplantar pustulosis (pustules, smokers), scabies (burrows), bullous pemphigoid (dyshidrosiform), herpes, hand-foot-mouth disease, dermatitis herpetiformis, EBS
- Hyperkeratotic hand eczema vs palmar psoriasis — psoriasis has sharper edges, other sites, nail pits; histology helps

**Q5. Investigations.**
- Detailed occupational and exposure history, look at feet (tinea), KOH, patch test (standard + occupational series) in every chronic hand eczema, prick test for contact urticaria, biopsy if psoriasis suspected

**Q6. Management of hand eczema.**
- Skin protection programme: avoid wet work >2 h/day, cotton-lined gloves, emollients after each wash, alcohol-based hand rubs preferable to soap
- Topical: potent steroids (clobetasol, mometasone) for short courses then intermittent; tacrolimus; delgocitinib cream (topical pan-JAK inhibitor approved for chronic hand eczema)
- Phototherapy: hand PUVA (topical psoralen) or NB-UVB
- Systemic: alitretinoin 30 mg/day for chronic hyperkeratotic hand eczema (teratogenic), acitretin (hyperkeratotic), short oral steroid for acute flares, cyclosporine, methotrexate, azathioprine, dupilumab (atopic hand eczema)
- Pompholyx: potassium permanganate soaks (1:10,000), potent steroid, drain large bullae, treat id source, botulinum toxin if hyperhidrosis, low-nickel diet if nickel-sensitive

**Q7. What is apron eczema?**
- Eczema on the proximal palm and adjacent volar surfaces of fingers — often allergic (food handlers) or atopic

**Q8. What is fingertip eczema?**
- Dry, fissured, scaly fingertips (pulpitis) — irritant (paper handlers), allergic (garlic — tulipalin/diallyl disulphide in chefs; Alstroemeria tulipalin in florists), atopic

**Q9. Prognosis?**
- Poor in atopics and when wet work continues; ~50% still have it after 15 years; early diagnosis, education and allergen avoidance improve outcome

## Quick spotter facts
- Tapioca-like deep vesicles on finger sides — pompholyx
- Chronic hand eczema — always patch test

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Hand eczema); ESCD hand eczema guideline. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
